name: jbig2dec
desc: JBIG2 decoder and library (for monochrome documents)
why: A decoder for JBIG2 documents, a format with a notoriously strange compression history worth exploring.

brief.what_it_is: jbig2dec is a decoder library plus a command-line example utility for JBIG2, the bi-level (monochrome) image compression format also known as ITU T.88 and ISO/IEC 14492. The jbig2dec command takes a JBIG2 file, or a pair of global and page streams, and decodes it. The README does not say what the output format is by default. The -o option names an output file.
brief.why_it_exists: The README says JBIG2 is included by reference in Adobe's PDF 1.4 and later, so PDF tooling that handles JBIG2 images needs a decoder. The project is also open to bug reports for files it cannot handle or renders wrongly.
brief.how_it_works: The README describes a command-line invocation that takes either one stream or two: a separate global stream and page stream, which it says are generally extracted from some embedded format. The README does not explain the internal decoding pipeline. The repository's file list shows separate modules for arithmetic, generic region, halftone, Huffman, MMR, refinement, symbol dictionary, text, and page/segment handling, with PBM and PNG image writers.

entry.title: jbig2dec
entry.tldr: A decoder for JBIG2, the monochrome image compression format hiding inside many scanned PDFs, with a command-line tool for unpacking streams.
entry.deeper_look:
jbig2dec is a decoder library plus a small example utility for JBIG2, the bi-level (black and white) image compression format, also known as ITU T.88 and ISO/IEC 14492. The `jbig2dec` command takes a JBIG2 file and decodes it. The `-o` option names the output file. The brief does not say what the default output format is.

The format matters because, per the README, JBIG2 is included by reference in Adobe's PDF 1.4 and later. Scanned documents in PDFs often carry JBIG2 images, so PDF tooling needs a decoder. This project exists to supply one.

The second invocation shows how JBIG2 lives inside other files. You can pass a global stream and a page stream separately, which the README says are generally extracted from some embedded format. JBIG2 is rarely a standalone file in practice. It is a pair of streams pulled out of a container.

The repository's file list suggests the structure of the spec. There are separate modules for arithmetic coding, generic regions, halftones, Huffman, MMR, refinement, symbol dictionaries, text regions, and page and segment handling, with PBM and PNG image writers. That makes the source a readable map of how a monochrome page can be split into symbols, regions, and halftones.

try_this.what_happens: Prints the usage text and the options the decoder accepts.
Decodes a single JBIG2 file into the named output file. Whether the format follows the extension is not stated in the brief, so check the result.
Decodes a global stream and a page stream together, as extracted from an embedded source such as a PDF.

entry.whats_unique: It is a small, focused decoder for a format that mostly hides inside PDFs, and its source is split along the spec's own building blocks.
entry.caveats: The README says the program is only partially functional and should be useful only in limited contexts, and the brief found no release dates.
